blockers: SECOPS-18 (w2-members / internal/devices): A device revoked in T0..T1 (peerM2D2) has member_devices.status='authorized' in the restored T0 database while NetBird N1 has already withdrawn it from fvpn-paid-<group_id> (with no external revocation tombstone in NetBird). When members.reconcile -> SyncMember -> SyncDevice (apps/worker/jobs_members.go:158, internal/devices/worker.go:72-93) runs after restore, it treats T0 member_devices.status='authorized' as authoritative and calls s.Adapter.SetAuthorization(ctx, deployment, peer, true, groups), silently re-adding the revoked peer to NetBird's paid group and re-including it in the node's active device_bindings without a discrepancy audit or re-confirmation.

node_retained_exposure.finding: node/agent/observe.go:111-116 sends a zeroed api.UsageOutboxStatus{} in POST /api/v1/agent/observations, and no node HTTP/CLI endpoint exposes retained ACKed usage records. The node persists all usage envelopes in /var/lib/vpn-node/state/usage.db (SQLite WAL tables: meta, events, ledger_epochs, replay_unavailable), keeping ACKed rows with state='archived' for DefaultArchiveRetain = 72h so ReconcileCheckpoint can un-archive and replay them when central rotates ledger_epoch during recovery.

fail_safe_negative_without_protocol.explanation: Without freeze/begin-recovery rotating ledger_epoch, events 3..5 remain state='archived' on the node (acked_through=5). While idle, Uploader.due() is false and nothing is sent. Once post-T1 traffic creates event > 5 in outbox, the node uploads only the new event under the old ledger_epoch; central advances max_seen_seq while returning highest_contiguous_seq=2, which the node rejects with ErrAckRegress ('usagestore: ack watermark cannot move backwards in the same epoch').

When members.reconcile (apps/worker/jobs_members.go:158 -> SyncMember -> SyncDevice in internal/devices/worker.go:72-93) runs after restore, it treats central member_devices.status='authorized' as authoritative and calls s.Adapter.SetAuthorization(ctx, deployment, peer, true, groups), silently re-authorizing the revoked peer in NetBird and restoring its forwarding without recording a revocation-discrepancy audit or requiring re-confirmation.
